# Zane Landers (AstroZane)

> Zane Landers is an amateur astronomer, telescope maker and science writer in Tucson, Arizona. He hosts private star parties in Tucson, Phoenix and across the Southwest through AstroZane, is Lead Writer and Editor of the telescope review site TelescopicWatch, writes for Live Science, serves on the founding board of DarkSky Southern Arizona and moderates r/telescopes.

## Star parties

- [Book a star party](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/): private, screen-free star parties for groups of 2 to 20, with hand-built telescopes and night vision. Bookings open January through May 2027 and August through December 2027; June and July by request only.
- [Tucson and Southern Arizona](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/tucson/): base price from $300 per group for one hour.
- [Phoenix and Scottsdale](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/phoenix/): base price from $500 per group, two-hour minimum, travel included.
- Larger events, Tucson area: from $500 for 21 to 40 guests, $700 for 41 to 70 and $950 for 71 to 100, with extra telescopes above 40.
- [Star parties for venues](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/venues/): resorts, hotels, guest ranches, vineyards, weddings and corporate events. Flat rate from $400 for two hours, recurring series from $250 a night, or ticketed with no cost up front. Venue dates open January through May 2027 and August through December 2027.
- [Sidewalk astronomy and public outreach](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/sidewalk-astronomy/): free looks at the Moon and planets on University Boulevard in Tucson and at public events, since 2022.
- [Telescope repair and setup help](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/telescope-repair/): in-person collimation, troubleshooting and repair in Tucson and Phoenix.
- [Contact](https://astrozane.com/links/contact/): booking requests, telescope repair, and writing or marketing work.

## Telescopes and astrophotography

- [Current telescopes](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/telescopes/)
- [14.7-inch f/2.9 Dobsonian](https://astrozane.com/projects/147-inch-f29/): hand-built main telescope.
- [24-inch f/4 Dobsonian](https://astrozane.com/projects/24-inch-f4/): a 2009 Eric Allen telescope being rebuilt, to be completed in 2027.
- 30-inch f/4.4 Starsplitter Dobsonian: shared with Cole Rees and kept at Chiricahua Sky Village. Not available for star parties.
- Also in use: a 1980 Celestron C8, an SVBONY MK127 and a ZWO SeeStar S50 Pro.
- Earlier builds: a 20.5-inch f/4.5 Dobsonian with a spray-silvered mirror, a 16-inch f/4.9 Dobsonian, a 10-inch f/3.2 Newtonian, and design work on the 3D-printed Hadley 114.
- Smart telescopes: has owned and reviewed nearly every smart telescope on the market for TelescopicWatch, including ZWO Seestar, Dwarf and Vaonis Vespera models.
- [Telescope FOV and magnification calculator](https://astrozane.com/calculators/FOV/)
- [Telescope limiting magnitude calculator](https://astrozane.com/calculators/limiting-magnitude/): faintest star or deep-sky surface brightness for a given telescope, sky and observer.
- [Astrophotography](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/astrophotography/)

## Elsewhere

- [TelescopicWatch](https://telescopicwatch.com/): hands-on telescope rankings, reviews and buying guides edited by Zane Landers.
- [Protecting dark skies in Tucson and Southern Arizona](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/dark-skies/): what threatens Tucson's night sky, what DarkSky International and DarkSky Southern Arizona each do, and how to help.
- [DarkSky Southern Arizona](https://darkskysoaz.org/): regional chapter of DarkSky International; donations at https://darkskysoaz.org/donate/.
- [Observational Astronomy Discord](https://discord.gg/astronomy): community for telescope help and observing.
- [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/astrozane): professional background; open to full-time marketing, communications and content roles.
